question: 400 guavas were bought at ₹1230 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹880. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of guavas.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Selling Price (SP) = (4 × 1230) + 880 = 4920 + 880 = ₹5800

Number of dozens in 400 guavas = 400 ÷ 12 = 100/3 dozens

SP per dozen = 5800 ÷ (100/3) = 5800 × 3 ÷ 100 = 174

**∴ The correct answer is ₹174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of guavas bought = 400

Cost price of 100 guavas = ₹1230

Profit earned = ₹880

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) of 400 guavas = 1230 × (400 ÷ 100)

⇒ Total CP = 1230 × 4 = ₹4920

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = Total CP + Profit

⇒ Total SP = 4920 + 880 = ₹5800

⇒ Total quantity in dozens = 400 ÷ 12 = 100/3 dozens

⇒ SP per dozen = Total SP ÷ Total dozens

⇒ SP per dozen = 5800 ÷ (100/3)

⇒ SP per dozen = 5800 × (3 ÷ 100) = ₹174

**∴ The correct answer is ₹174.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method

This method determines the value of a standard unit (like one item or a dozen) from the given multiple quantity, which can then be applied to find the equivalent proportional value.

Profit and Loss Basics

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) + Profit. Profit occurs when SP > CP. If CP is greater than SP, it results in a Loss.

Dozen Conversion

1 Dozen = 12 items. To convert a specific number of individual items into dozens, simply divide the total item count by 12.
